assumptions: Because no structured SpecJson states were provided, Manual was chosen as the initial mode from the NL description of manual and autocontrol pump modes.
Ask_StartAC setpoint modification is represented by an external integer setpoint_delta applied during Ask_StartAC; the NL does not name a specific setpoint-change event.
AutocontrolInit is modeled as progressing to AutocontrolNormal by an unconditional transition because the NL names AutocontrolInit and normal autocontrol but does not specify the completion trigger.
The blood-pressure-to-flow computation is a simple monotonic abstraction: pressure above target lowers flow relative to default_flow_rate, and pressure below target raises it.
Display and audible error messages are abstracted as the alarm_signal variable because the NL does not provide separate display and sound command names.

grounding_seeds.evidence_text: In the Mode_Control_Algorithm hierarchy, CARA has manual and autocontrol-related mode-control states plus an Ask_StartAC submode.
The pump has manual and autocontrol modes. In manual mode, pump speed is set with the built-in switch.
CARA has ... an Ask_StartAC submode; within Ask_StartAC, the setpoint can be changed and pressing StartAC enters AutocontrolInit.
During normal autocontrol, CARA controls flow rate only while there are no pump-operation complications.
If a pump fault such as fluid-tubing occlusion occurs, the pump activates alarm signals, the caregiver removes the fault.
The Caregiver Interface lets the caregiver ... initiate ... algorithmic pump control.
within Ask_StartAC ... pressing StartAC enters AutocontrolInit.

repair_rationale: The selected model-review failure is unsafe_recovery: cp_backmanual_from_fault could reach Manual with pump_fault = 1 but alarm_signal = 0 because Manual.enter cleared the alarm unconditionally.

When there is no fault, pump_fault = 0, so ordinary entry to Manual and TerminateAC recovery still produce alarm_signal = 0. This preserves the prior repaired scenario autocontrol_init_terminate_and_pump_fault_paths because AutocontrolInit -> Manual :: TerminateAC remains ordered before the unconditional AutocontrolInit -> AutocontrolNormal transition.

The caregiver fault-removal path remains Fault -> Manual :: FaultCleared with pump_fault = 0 and alarm_signal = 0, preserving the NL requirement that alarms clear when the caregiver removes the fault.

All required grounded elements are preserved, including the Mode_Control_Algorithm hierarchy, Manual, Ask_StartAC, AutocontrolInit, AutocontrolNormal, Fault, InitiateAC, StartAC, TerminateAC, PumpFault, FaultCleared, all four backManual events, the no-pump-fault guard in AutocontrolNormal, pump-fault transitions, and the manual/autocontrol pump actions.
